בִּשְׁגָגָה is carried by the single word unwittingly, so the preposition shares that word's unit (rule 30), and the construction-supplied copula with its dummy subject — it was — joins that prepositional predicate (rules 20, 49). The unit is discontinuous around the supplied done under rule 25.

done is a whole lexical verb supplied for a clause whose Hebrew writes none: כִּי לְכָל־הָעָם בִּשְׁגָגָה has no verb, and rule 20 covers only the copula and a presentative dummy, so no morpheme licenses it (rules 20, 30). This is the חֲמַס אֶרֶץ → violence done to the land case: done predicates an event rather than completing any morpheme's rendering. Reading it was done whole as the fused phrase's construction frame was the competing analysis, rejected because a clause with no verb in it licenses no verb.

Both datives of the forgiveness clause are recast as English subjects and go unrepresented (rule 40).
